Keepplacementranges and95%startcriterion.

The conservative release-at-first-contact sampler holds 237/256 starts (pose30208), below the 95% start check. TASK.md says a person sets the cube in the palm before asking; first-contact release can instead balance it on the leading finger. I will compare a physically simulated gentle placement: a limited user wrench before episode time zero guides the cube toward the sampled palm region, fades out, then the same fixed hand holds it force-free for two seconds. No object wrench is permitted in policy episodes; every failed placement remains a failed start, and sampling ranges/criteria stay unchanged.

Prototype compliant-corner test exposed 9.24mm overlaps between the internal core inertia sphere and solid convex corner proxies. These were previously excluded by adjacent-body filtering in the rigid reduction, but became active on grandchild corner bodies and drove unphysical twists. Before recording simulation or training, disabled collision on the internal inertia carrier; actual corner-corner and hand-corner contacts remain. Will rerun compliant starts and document the retained-joint mechanism limitation.

The packaged hold evaluator passes the standard hand-supported start check on64/64 dev seeds with five edge sizes48–52mm,mass50–90g,mu.4–1.2 and passive-mechanism variation; no hardware violations. An analytical DLS thumb approach achieves0/8 opposed grips. Logged pad positions show it tracks a poor local IK branch and pushes the cube forward. FK also corrects my wrist-roll sign intuition: delta-.15 gives palm tilt76.5deg, while positive delta flattens it.
